q: He no longer can fall asleep without one of us in the same room as him. He’s been waking at 2am and is up for sometimes 90 minutes with nothing we can do to calm him down. He used to have no sleep issues
cx: Parent of a just-3-year-old at a foreign-language daycare; sleep changed with new behaviour at school.

q: Over the past 10 months, he (and my wife and I) have never slept more than 4 hours at a time. Most nights he's waking up 4-6 times AT A MINIMUM. Sometimes as much as 8-12 times.
cx: Father of an almost 10-month-old, title: the paediatrician is pissing me off.

q: the first thing she said was that she probably wouldn't be referring us to a sleep professional, because those types of doctors are for kids with actual sleep conditions like insomnia.
cx: The paediatrician's answer to their request for a sleep referral.

q: Due to my uncertainty with some questions, she said the issue was that his schedule wasn't tight enough. […] Basically that every day should be a carbon copy of the day before. […] In the past month, absolutely NOTHING has changed with his night time sleep.
cx: They followed the doctor's tighter-schedule advice for a month.

q: Instead of giving a definitive timeline, she said "Well, at some point, one of you will give up. Either he will, or you will (meaning us, his parents)". I don't understand what kind of answer that is. You're putting the entire burden on my and my wife's endurance.
cx: He asked when they would re-evaluate if the schedule still did not work.

q: Not a single one of them has had to map out their kids day LITERALLY minute by minute to stop them from waking up 10 times per night.
cx: Comparing with the mothers he knows.

q: We aren't enjoying our son like we should be during this period. Sleep shouldn't be this hard. […] Our schedule with him is already 50x more strict than every other family we know and somehow he still sleeps worse than all of them.
cx: End of his post.

q: We keep getting told the opposite. We keep hearing that our son is constantly in a state of being overtired, which causes cortisol and adrenaline to be going through his system constantly
cx: A commenter suggested more sleep pressure; others had said overtired.

q: I think a lot of my frustration with this subreddit is everyone just keeps saying "do sleep training", but they never elaborate on which. It's like if my car broke down and I went to a mechanic subreddit asking for help and everyone just replied with "just fix it".
cx: The exact-steps complaint about the forum's standard reply.

q: Cry it out bothers her for a multitude of reasons; the biggest being that she feels like she's abandoning her child. […] My wife is still hesitant, but I think she's about to hit her breaking point.
cx: The father on his wife's view of crying-it-out.

q: Around 8 months, he started rejecting me at night. If I was trying to soothe him, he would scream his head off forever until my wife eventually woke up from the noise and came in the room.
cx: Why his wife now does 90% of the nights.

q: We live in a fairly small condo, so when he starts screaming, there's no chance of anyone in the house sleeping. So once the screaming starts, we're both awake.
cx: Space as the reason split nights do not work.

q: Trust me, I've done hours and hours of research into everything surrounding his sleep. My question wasn't "what is sleep training" or "what sleep training should I do?" My question was "What sleep training did YOU do?"
cx: He wants other parents' own cases, not general advice.

q: I cannot FORCE him to sleep for an hour if he wakes up at 30 minutes. I cannot FORCE him to fall asleep at a specific time. The only time-related aspect of his sleep that I can somewhat control is his wake times.
cx: Two days later, still answering schedule advice.

q: I'm entering a mentally demanding and competitive program in the fall and really think I need to be sleeping through the night to give myself the best shot. Bub will be 16 months when I start. He still wakes up frequently in the night to nurse (dont want to sleep train).
cx: Breastfeeding mother of a 13-month-old ending maternity leave; a deadline drives the ask.

q: It's honestly hard to comfort him for anything (falls, frustration, etc.,) without milk but I do successfully redirect him maybe 50% of the time. His dad has had some successes putting him down for naps or bed without milk
cx: Same mother: what has worked so far.

q: FTM here and I am CONSUMED by my baby’s sleep schedule. I’m overwhelmed by the “experts” and the apps and the influencers selling sleep programs. I’m tired of hearing the phrases “drowsy by wake” or “wake windows” or “sleep pressure” or the differences between “undertired vs. overtired.”
cx: First-time mother of a 5-month-old, title: 5 months of baby sleep schedule obsession.

q: Is anyone out there just winging their baby’s sleep? Not following a schedule, wake windows or guidelines from research? Just simply listening to their baby. If so, how’s it going?
cx: Her ask.

q: I desperately need to get my life back and not be so freaking consumed by my baby’s sleep schedule. But I also want her (and me) to sleep.
cx: Same post.

q: I switched to logging naps on a whiteboard to help me feel a little less addicted to a baby app. It helps a little bit that an app isn’t pressuring me about naps lol
cx: Her own fix for app pressure, toggling between three and four naps.

q: Daycare nap: 1 PM–3 PM (non-negotiable, center-based daycare) […] **He proceeds to party until 11:00–11:30 PM.**
cx: Mother of a just-3-year-old and a newborn; the daycare nap pushes bedtime late.

q: My daycare kinda (very subtly) refused, saying it will disturb the class 😥
cx: Asked the daycare to shorten the nap.

q: I have a tiny mom-guilt angel on one shoulder saying, “He’s only 3 once, soak up every moment,” while the exhausted mom on the other shoulder is holding a bottle brush, packing daycare bags, and wondering why everyone in this house is awake at 10 PM.
cx: Same mother replying to tips.

q: We actually haven’t tried moving bedtime up significantly because, in my head, a child who naps until 3 PM shouldn’t possibly be ready for bed at 8 PM. 😅 Clearly, though, my logic and my toddler’s operating system may not be running the same software.
cx: A commenter's detailed reply changed her plan.

q: How are we resolving the issue of partner not taking over night shift? Like no matter the circumstances, he will not do it. Is the only option leaving the relationship and being a single mom??
cx: Mother with a fever asking her fiancé to do one night.

q: I tried venting to friends but they say I’m dramatic and it’s a moms job to take care of baby lol to say I’ve been feeling alone is an understatement
cx: What her friends said.

q: it’s 5am and I have had the baby with me all night, she woke up wanting a bottle so I go into the other bedroom to wake up fiancé and tell him that he slept enough and needs to take over…. This man says to me “I caught what you have and I’m too sick, can you just close the door?”
cx: Her update at 5am.

q: I was always firmly against CIO because, as a therapist, I understand attachment. But the longer he goes with horrible sleep, the more exhausted and frustrated I’ve become.
cx: Parent of a 15-month-old who has to be rocked to sleep.

q: I’ve tried gentle sleep training where I put him down drowsy and let him cry, but for no longer than 10 minutes. Only twice in the last month has he put himself down while I hide in the corner of the room. 😂
cx: Same parent, naps under an hour and blamed on the 15-month regression.

q: I feel like I’m being forced to sleep train him. Literally most of the mom friends I have react so weird when I say I don’t plan to.
cx: Breastfeeding first-time mother of a 5-month-old who wakes twice and is content.

q: He’s ebf and wakes up twice at night to eat and goes right back to sleep. I don’t mind to get up with him at all. […] I cherish every moment with him since he’s my first and I don’t want to stop rocking him to sleep.
cx: The content non-trainer's side.

q: Right around the time she turned two, it’s like a switch flipped and sleep changed. […] When this started happening, I assumed it was a developmental sleep regression so we didn’t make any changes. It has now been six months of the late bedtimes.
cx: Parent of a 2.5-year-old, sleep trained at 4.5 months; daycare nap and bedtime clash.

q: While I don’t mind sitting with her to fall asleep, there’s something sooo frustrating about sitting there FOREVER with her seemingly not tired at all 😅😭
cx: The bedtime scene.

q: Have we misread the whole situation and she has needed an earlier bedtime the entire time because of extra stimulation at daycare, once she moved to the daycare centre, and is actually overtired which is causing her to put up a fight at bedtime?
cx: Her over- versus undertired question.

q: She would barely nap there snd fought every bottle she was given. […] I wanted to quit my job and pull her out after the first week […] Well, we’re 2.5 months in and she is doing SO much better. Her naps are still shorter there than at home (30-35mins usually)
cx: Positive daycare story from a parent whose baby started at 13 weeks.
